story.head: Reinhart’s favorite opponent
paras: The Panthers already played in Columbus once this season and left with a 7-3 win on Oct 13. The Panthers (9-5-2) beat Chicago 5-3 on Wednesday, while the Blue Jackets (7-8-0) lost 5-2 to Buffalo on Friday. Going in, the Panthers are fifth in the Atlantic (tied for 11th in the NHL) and the Blue Jackets sixth in the Metropolitan (27th).
This season, the Blue Jackets have been outscored 47-38, but only 28-25 at 5-on-5. On special teams, opponents have outscored them 12-7.

The Panthers forecheck harder than anyone (1st), hit a lot (1st) and kill penalties well (1st). On the other side, the Blue Jackets get their defensemen shooting (4th) and get a lot of their shots blocked (29th). They also get pinned in their own end on long shifts (28th), so the Panthers’ forecheck could keep them pinned in their own end. The Cats’ power play (3rd) could do real damage against the Blue Jackets’ penalty kill (27th).

Matthew Tkachuk (4 G / 18 A / 22 P in 16 GP) leads the Panthers in scoring, with seven points in his last five games and a point in six straight games against Columbus. Sam Reinhart (9 G / 7 A / 16 P in 16 GP) has a team-high nine goals, with eight points in his last five games. For the Blue Jackets, Kent Johnson (8 G / 8 A / 16 P in 15 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Zach Werenski (2 G / 12 A / 14 P in 15 GP) is next in line.

Jacob Markström (4-2-1 / .885 SV% in 8 GS) will likely start for Florida. Columbus has two options in net: Jet Greaves (2-6-0 / .879 SV% in 8 GS) and Cam Talbot (5-2-0 / .909 SV% in 7 GS). They have split the last ten starts, and Greaves got the last one on Friday. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.
At home, Rick Bowness likes to send Sillinger, Coyle and Olivier out against the other team’s top line, so watch for them against B. Tkachuk, Bennett and M. Tkachuk.
